user.title: Connect to your Visonic alarm
user.description:
This connects through the **same cloud service as the Visonic GO or Connect Alarm app** — not directly to the panel. You need a working app login first: if you cannot sign in to the app, this will not work either.

Two different things are needed, and they are easy to mix up:

- your **app account** (email + password), which you chose when you registered
- your **panel** (serial + keypad PIN), which identifies the alarm itself

Everything below can be found in the app under the panel settings, or in the welcome email from whoever installed or monitors your alarm.

data_description.host: The server your alarm reports to. Most UK and European panels use the default, visonic.tycomonitor.com. If your alarm is professionally monitored, your provider may use a different one — it is shown in the app's About or Server screen.
data_description.user_email: The email you sign in to the Visonic GO or Connect Alarm app with. Not an installer or engineer account.
data_description.user_password: The password for that app account. This is not your keypad PIN.
data_description.panel_id: A short code such as 1D0B0A, usually 6 characters. Find it in the app under panel settings, on the sticker inside the panel, or in your welcome email. Sometimes called the panel ID or panel serial.
data_description.user_code: The PIN you type on the keypad to disarm the alarm, normally 4 digits. Use your own user code, not the installer or engineer code — the integration arms and disarms as that user, so it is the one that shows up in the event log.
data_description.app_id: Leave this blank. One is generated for you. Only fill it in if you are moving an existing setup and need to keep the same client identifier.

reauth_confirm.title: Re-authenticate {panel}
reauth_confirm.description:
Visonic rejected the stored credentials for **{panel}**.

This usually means the app account password was changed, or the keypad PIN was changed on the panel. Enter the current details to reconnect.

data_description.user_password: The password for your Visonic GO or Connect Alarm account, not your keypad PIN.
data_description.user_code: The PIN you type on the keypad to disarm.

reconfigure.title: Reconfigure your Visonic alarm
reconfigure.description:
Change how Home Assistant reaches the panel.

This has to stay pointed at the **same panel** — the serial number cannot be changed here. To add a different alarm, add a second integration instead.

data_description.host: Only change this if your monitoring provider has moved you to a different server.
data_description.user_code: The PIN you type on the keypad to disarm.

error.cannot_connect: Could not reach that server. Check the monitoring server address is spelled correctly and that Home Assistant has internet access.
error.invalid_auth: Visonic rejected those details. The most common causes are using the keypad PIN as the account password, a mistyped panel serial, or an installer code instead of your own user code. Confirm the same details work in the Visonic GO or Connect Alarm app.
error.unknown: Unexpected error. Check the Home Assistant log for details.

abort.already_configured: This panel is already set up.
abort.cannot_connect: Could not reach the Visonic server, so the YAML configuration was not imported.
abort.invalid_auth: The credentials in your YAML configuration were rejected, so it was not imported.
abort.unknown: Unexpected error importing the YAML configuration.
abort.wrong_panel: Those credentials are for a different panel. Reconfiguring must keep the same panel.

init.title: Visonic Alarm options
init.description: These only affect Home Assistant. Nothing here is written to the panel.

data.no_pin_required: Arm and disarm without entering the code

data_description.no_pin_required: Turn this on to skip the code prompt in Home Assistant, so dashboard buttons and automations can arm or disarm directly. Your keypad PIN is still sent to the panel either way — this only controls whether Home Assistant asks you to type it first. Leave it off if anyone who can reach your dashboard should not be able to disarm the alarm.
data_description.event_hour_offset: Only needed if the times on the Last event sensor look wrong, which happens when the panel's clock is set to a different time zone. Enter the number of hours to shift them by, positive or negative.

refresh.name: Refresh
refresh.description: Polls the panel immediately instead of waiting for the next scheduled update.

sound_siren.name: Sound siren
sound_siren.description: Sounds the siren as a panic alarm. This is loud and immediate.

config_entry_id.name: Panel
config_entry_id.description: The Visonic panel whose siren should sound.

config_entry_id.name: Panel
config_entry_id.description: The Visonic panel whose siren should be silenced.

mode.name: Mode
mode.description: Which sounders to silence. Defaults to all.

set_zone_name.name: Set zone name
set_zone_name.description: Renames a zone on the panel itself, not just in Home Assistant.

zone.name: Zone number
zone.description: The panel zone number, shown as the zone attribute on each zone entity.

cannot_connect.message: Could not reach the Visonic server: {error}

invalid_code.message: The code you entered is not correct.

not_ready.message: The alarm is not ready to arm. There may be a door or window open.

zone_unavailable.message: That zone is no longer enrolled on the panel.

entry_not_loaded.message: The Visonic panel {target} is not loaded.

yaml_deprecated.title: Visonic Alarm YAML configuration is deprecated
yaml_deprecated.description:
Visonic Alarm is now set up from the user interface. Your existing YAML configuration has been imported, and all entity IDs were preserved.

Remove the `visonicalarm:` block from `configuration.yaml` and restart Home Assistant to clear this message. Your credentials are now stored in the config entry, so they no longer need to live in `secrets.yaml` for this integration.

panel_offline.title: {panel} is not reporting to the Visonic cloud
panel_offline.description:
The alarm panel has stopped communicating with the monitoring server. The cloud keeps serving the **last known** arm state, so the alarm entity will look normal while being out of date — any automation that trusts it is now working from stale data.

Check the panel's broadband or GPRS connection. If the panel has an IP address but still cannot connect, confirm which server address it is configured to report to.
